title: Gloria in excelsis - aria with very long melismas (Latin)

expected.notes: Two parts: Soprano (one staff, all lyrics) and Piano (ONE part with two staves - never split into RH/LH parts). 34 syllables, all lyric number 1. Melismas: "a" of Gloria (14 notes), "o" of Deo (21 notes, crosses a system break), "pax" (20 notes incl. a tie, crosses a system break), "lu" of the first Alleluia (9 notes, hyphenated melisma: syllabic middle, no extend). Word-final melismas carry <extend/>. Melisma notes must NOT receive lyric elements. Beams are left to LilyPond (truth has no <beam>).

expected.notes: Single melody part. Verse section (bars 1-8): four stacked lines, lyric numbers 1-4. title: Calon Lân - closed SATB with four independent lyric lines (Welsh)

expected.notes: Closed score, 2 staves x 2 voices -> 4 parts. Each voice sings DIFFERENT words with its own rhythm, and each has its own lyric line: Soprano text ABOVE the treble staff, Alto text BELOW the treble staff, Tenor text ABOVE the bass staff (so two lines sit between the staves: upper = Alto, lower = Tenor), Bass text BELOW the bass staff. Every part has lyric number 1. Attaching a line to the wrong voice (e.g. the Alto line to the Tenor) is an error. Welsh â and apostrophes (wy'n, na'r, na'i, nu'r) must be kept.

title: Amazing Grace - hymnal page, stanzas 4-6 as text block below the music

expected.notes: Closed SATB hymn -> 4 parts. Stanzas 1-3 are underlaid between the staves and belong to the SOPRANO (lyric numbers 1-3). Stanzas 4-6 are printed as a two-column TEXT BLOCK below the music: they are not aligned to notes, so truth.musicxml carries them as <credit> elements (credit-type "lyrics", one per stanza, label + lines). truth-underlaid.musicxml is an alternative truth for converters that syllabify the block and underlay it as lyric lines 4-6 (it has no credits). Pencil marks, circled notes and handwritten words ("breathe", "rit." ...) in the scans are NOT part of the music or lyrics. Apostrophes are typographic (U+2019).

title: Tu scendi dalle stelle - Italian elisions, voice and piano

expected.notes: Two parts: Canto (voice, 2 stanzas = lyric numbers 1-2) and Pianoforte (ONE part, two staves - never split). Elisions (two or three syllables sung on one note, joined by the elision tie "‿") are a single <lyric> with <elision> between the <text> parts, e.g. "do‿e‿al" = text do (end) + elision + e (single) + elision + al (single). Do not split an elided group over several notes and do not drop the parts after the tie. Apostrophes (l'a-, m'in-) and accents (stò, tà, più, ché) must be kept.
